title: Wedding List
source: Midnight Bet — Integrated ARC I — Old Friends, New Heat
paragraphs: The wedding belonged to Rhea’s cousin.
Still, Saturday morning found Mira, Rhea, Naina, Aarav, Kabir and Dev in Neha and Arjun’s living room surrounded by lists.
Holi supplies for the pre-wedding weekend.
Rhea sat cross-legged on the floor in soft shorts that rode high on her thighs when she shifted.
Arjun stood behind her chair reading a list over her shoulder.
The heat of his body reached her back. The soft fabric of his shirt brushed her hair when he leaned.
Neha was on the sofa calling a vendor.
Rhea could feel Arjun’s presence before his hand reached past her for the pen.
His forearm brushed her bare shoulder.
Warm. Firm. Lingering half a second longer than necessary.
The place where his skin had touched hers stayed warm.
Across the room, Mira watched Aarav argue with Neha about music.
He wore a white T-shirt that fitted close across his chest and shoulders. The fabric stretched when he gestured.
Mira noticed the line of his arms, the way the cotton sat against his body.
Mehul and Sana arrived carrying boxes.
Mehul wore sunglasses and a dark shirt open at the throat.
Mira noticed him too — the calm set of his shoulders, the way his hands looked when he set the boxes down.
His argument with Neha became unnecessarily intense.
Kabir came from the kitchen with Tara.
Rohan had dropped her and gone to work.
Her eyes landed on Tara’s hand at Kabir’s elbow — soft fingers resting against his skin, the silver anklet catching light when she walked.
Dev sat beside Naina making a spreadsheet.
Their knees touched under the coffee table.
The warm pressure of Naina’s thigh against his stayed deliberate.
Shalini’s lesson from the day before sat in Dev’s body.
The wedding list became pair assignments.
Nothing was random enough to feel safe.
The first task took Aarav and Sana to the airport.
She wore a sleeveless rust top that left her arms bare and the soft upper curves of her breasts visible when she turned the wheel.
Aarav noticed her arms. The smooth skin. The way the fabric shifted against her chest with every movement.
At a red light she looked at him.
Aarav did not know what to do with that.
“Those are not the same as permission.”
At the market, Mira walked beside Mehul choosing décor fabric.
They stood at the same rack.
But the heat of his body at her shoulder was clear. The faint scent of his cologne. The solid presence of a man who was not Aarav and not careful about it.
Mira felt the warmth at her shoulder.
The fact he asked stayed with her.
Their hands overlapped on the cardboard.
His fingers warm against hers. Broad. Steady.
The contact of their hands lasted a second longer than needed before he released.
Across the city, Kabir and Tara entered a guest room with fresh sheets.
Tara knelt to open a storage box.
The movement made her top shift, showing the soft curve of her lower back and the way her trousers sat low on her hips.
Close enough that he could see the faint shadow between her breasts under the thin fabric of her top.
Tara reached past him for the blanket.
Her body brushed his arm — soft breast against his bicep through the fabric, the heat of her skin clear for one full second.
Then she took the blanket and stepped back.
The room felt smaller than it had a minute ago.
Rhea and Arjun drove invitation cards across town.
She watched his hand on the steering wheel.
At a traffic light, Arjun said:
Rhea looked down at her shirt.
Rhea liked the unanswered question too much.
Dev and Naina worked at the dining table.
Naina rested her head briefly near his shoulder to see the screen.
His hand tightened on the mouse.
“Means you are not made of stone.”
Then her knee pressed slightly more firmly against his.
Later that evening, all assignments returned to the same living room.
Aarav saw Mira carrying boxes with Mehul.
Mira saw Sana sitting too comfortably beside Aarav.
Kabir saw Rhea return with Arjun smiling.
Rhea saw Tara leave a hand on Kabir’s shoulder while explaining sheets.
Dev saw Naina glance at his phone when Shalini’s name appeared.
Everyone had spent the day in separate pairings.
Arjun put an arm around Neha.
Instead it sharpened the forbidden edges.
At 10 p.m., the core six left together.
Dev and Naina behind them in another car.
At the first red light, Kabir said:
Now silence belonged to four people.
Attraction was no longer a neat map of school friends.
And every future game would carry those outside memories inside it.
